meta.titre: Price Quotations and Delivery Terms: who pays for carriage, loading and insurance
meta.sous_theme: Quotations, ex-works, carriage paid, carriage forward, FOB and CIF

sections.contenu_markdown: A cement dealer in Limbe asks two suppliers for prices. One says 'ex-works' and the other says 'delivered'. The first price looks lower, but a lorry, labourers and insurance have to be paid for, so the cheaper-looking offer may cost more in the end. Delivery terms decide who pays each cost on the way from seller to buyer. The GCE Commerce papers often ask what a given term means and who pays loading or carriage, so you must know each one precisely.

items: A buyer sends an enquiry to ask a seller for prices.
Goods are moved from the seller to the buyer by transport, and they may be insured against loss or damage on the way.
A trade discount is a reduction on the list price given to businesses that buy to resell.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Quotation
A **quotation** is the seller's reply to a buyer's enquiry. It states the goods, quantity, price, trade discount and cash discount if any, delivery terms, delivery time, payment terms and how long the offer stays open. It is an offer to sell: when the buyer places an order that accepts it, a contract exists. A phrase such as **E. & O.E.** (errors and omissions excepted) lets the seller correct a genuine mistake in the quotation.

### Delivery terms
| Term | Meaning | Seller pays | Buyer pays |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ex-works** (ex-factory, ex-warehouse) | Price of goods at the seller's own premises, such as the manufacturer's warehouse | Nothing beyond preparing the goods | Loading, transport, insurance and every cost from there |
| **Carriage paid** (free delivery) | Price includes delivery to the buyer's address | Carriage to the buyer | Nothing extra for carriage |
| **Carriage forward** | Price does not include carriage | Nothing for carriage | Carriage, paid when the goods arrive |
| **FOB** (free on board) | Price includes getting the goods onto the ship at the port named | Costs up to and including **loading on board** | Freight, insurance and later charges |
| **CIF** (cost, insurance, freight) | Price includes the cost of goods, insurance and freight to the destination port | Goods, insurance and freight | Charges after arrival, such as import duty |

### Comparing quotations
The lowest unit price is not always the cheapest offer. Add to each quotation every extra cost the buyer must pay, then compare the **total cost to the buyer**.

$$\text{Total cost to buyer} = \text{Price of goods} + \text{Carriage} + \text{Loading} + \text{Insurance} \ (\text{the ones the buyer pays})$$

Also look at the trade discount, the credit period and the delivery time before choosing.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks what a quotation contains or what to check before ordering.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Check the description and quantity, the price per unit, any discounts, the **delivery term**, the delivery date, the payment terms and the period for which the quotation is valid. A quotation is for particular goods requested by a buyer, while a catalogue or price list is sent to many customers.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question mentions a port, a ship or a foreign buyer.
variantes.contenu_markdown: FOB and CIF are used when goods travel by sea. Ex-works, carriage paid and carriage forward are common in home trade. An exporter who quotes **FOB Douala** pays to get the goods on board at Douala, and the overseas buyer pays what follows.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for the difference between two terms.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Contrast the point at which cost passes to the buyer. Under ex-works it passes at the seller's premises, under FOB when the goods are on the ship, under CIF at the destination port for freight and insurance, and under carriage paid at delivery.

sections.enonce_markdown: A hardware shop in Limbe needs 200 bags of cement. Supplier A quotes 10,000 FCFA per bag ex-works. The shop would pay 60,000 FCFA for transport, 20,000 FCFA for loading and 15,000 FCFA for insurance. Supplier B quotes 10,400 FCFA per bag as a delivered price, with carriage and insurance paid by the supplier. Calculate the total cost of each offer and state which one the shop should choose on price alone.

etapes.action: Find the price of the goods from Supplier A
etapes.justification: Price of goods = number of bags x price per bag.

etapes.action: Add the costs the shop pays under ex-works terms
etapes.justification: With ex-works, the buyer pays transport, loading and insurance.

etapes.action: Find the total cost of Supplier B
etapes.justification: The delivered price already includes carriage and insurance, so nothing is added.
The cheapest offer is the one with the lowest total cost to the buyer.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Supplier A costs 2,095,000 FCFA in all and Supplier B costs 2,080,000 FCFA. Supplier B is cheaper by 15,000 FCFA even though its price per bag is higher, because Supplier A's ex-works price leaves several costs to the buyer.

items.erreur_markdown: Ex-works means the seller delivers the goods to the buyer's shop.
items.pourquoi_faux: Ex-works is the price of the goods at the seller's own premises. The buyer collects them and pays for everything after that.
items.correction_markdown: Ex-works: the buyer pays loading, transport and insurance. It is **carriage paid** that includes delivery to the buyer.

items.erreur_markdown: Under carriage forward, the seller pays the carriage.
items.pourquoi_faux: Carriage forward means the carriage is still to come and is paid by the buyer when the goods are received.
items.correction_markdown: Carriage forward: **buyer** pays. Carriage paid: **seller** pays.

items.erreur_markdown: In an FOB quotation, the buyer pays the loading charges at the port.
items.pourquoi_faux: The FOB price includes the cost of getting the goods on board the ship, loading included.
items.correction_markdown: Under FOB the **seller** pays the loading charges. The buyer pays the freight and insurance from the ship onward.

items.erreur_markdown: The supplier with the lowest price per unit is always the cheapest.
items.pourquoi_faux: A low ex-works price can hide transport, loading and insurance costs which the buyer must add.
items.correction_markdown: Calculate the total cost to the buyer for each quotation, then compare.

items.erreur_markdown: A CIF price does not include insurance, so the buyer must insure the goods on the voyage.
items.pourquoi_faux: The letters CIF stand for cost, insurance and freight, and all three are included in the seller's price up to the destination port.
items.correction_markdown: CIF includes cost, insurance and freight. FOB is the term where the buyer arranges freight and insurance.

items.enonce_markdown: A trader in Bafoussam is quoted 1,200,000 FCFA ex-works for a set of tables. She must pay 85,000 FCFA for carriage and 15,000 FCFA for insurance. Who pays the loading charges, and what is her total cost?
items.solution_markdown:
The buyer pays the loading charges, because an ex-works price covers only the goods at the seller's premises.
Total cost $= 1\,200\,000 + 85\,000 + 15\,000 = 1\,300\,000$ FCFA.
**The buyer pays loading; total cost 1,300,000 FCFA.**

items.enonce_markdown: A school needs desks. Supplier A has a list price of 5,000,000 FCFA less a trade discount of 10%, carriage paid. Supplier B has a list price of 4,800,000 FCFA less a trade discount of 10%, ex-works. The school would pay Supplier B's loading (40,000 FCFA), transport (180,000 FCFA) and insurance (30,000 FCFA). Calculate the total cost of each offer and say which is cheaper.

An exporter quotes a foreign buyer 8,000,000 FCFA for a consignment of timber, FOB Douala. The sea freight to the buyer's port is 450,000 FCFA and the insurance for the voyage is 80,000 FCFA. (a) Who pays the loading charges at Douala? (b) What would the CIF price be if the exporter quoted the delivered-to-port cost instead? (c) The buyer pays freight and insurance herself under FOB. What is her total cost for goods, freight and insurance? (d) Name one reason why a buyer might prefer FOB and one why she might prefer CIF.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The **exporter** pays, since an FOB price includes getting the goods on board.
(b) CIF price $= 8\,000\,000 + 450\,000 + 80\,000 = 8\,530\,000$ FCFA.
(c) The buyer's total under FOB $= 8\,000\,000 + 450\,000 + 80\,000 = 8\,530\,000$ FCFA. The total is the same, but under FOB she arranges and pays freight and insurance herself.
(d) FOB: she may choose her own shipping line and insurer, possibly at lower cost or with better service. CIF: the seller arranges freight and insurance, so the buyer has less to organise and one price to compare.
**Exporter pays loading; CIF price 8,530,000 FCFA; buyer's total 8,530,000 FCFA.**

items_markdown: A quotation is a seller's reply to an enquiry, giving price, terms of delivery, payment terms and the period for which it is valid.
Ex-works: price at the seller's premises, the buyer pays loading, transport and insurance. Carriage paid: seller pays delivery. Carriage forward: buyer pays on arrival.
FOB: the seller pays up to and including loading on board; the buyer pays freight and insurance. CIF: the seller's price includes cost, insurance and freight to the destination port.
Compare quotations by the total cost to the buyer, adding all extra costs, not by the price per unit alone.
Also compare trade discount, payment terms and delivery time before choosing a supplier.
